channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Dispute with Ministry of Health Leaves Visually Impaired Woman Without Necessary Medication
item.description: A visually impaired woman, a first-group invalid, has been struggling to obtain necessary medication for Bechterew's disease for two years. After exhausting personal savings, she sought state assistance but received conflicting medical opinions. The woman believes the drug helps preserve her vision and prevent further deterioration.

item.title: Nazarbayev Order Removed from Book of Glory List
item.description: The Nazarbayev Order has been removed from the list of nominations for the Book of Glory. No further details were provided regarding the reasons for this decision or the implications.

item.title: Bishkek Village to Experience 10-Hour Water Outage on November 20
item.description: The village of Selektsionnom in Bishkek will have its drinking water supply temporarily cut off for 10 hours on November 20, from 10:00 to 20:00. The interruption is to connect a new 273-millimeter pipeline on Makhatma Gandhi Street. Residents are advised to store water.

item.title: British Authorities Transfer US Army Officer Arrested for Espionage to US Military
item.description: British police have transferred a US Army officer, arrested on suspicion of espionage in western England, to a US military detention facility. The officer is being questioned over allegations related to national security. Russia has denied any involvement in the case.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan MP: Residents of Uncommissioned Buildings Should Not Pay Commercial Utility Tariffs
item.description: Elvira Surabaldieva, a Member of the Kyrgyz Parliament, stated that residents of multi-apartment buildings not yet commissioned should not be charged commercial utility tariffs. She argued that residents are not at fault for construction delays and that higher tariffs are unaffordable for many.

item.title: Saudi-Led Coalition Destroys 60 Houthi Military Targets in Yemen
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition announced the destruction of 60 Houthi military targets across Yemen, including tunnels used for ballistic missile storage. The operation targeted Houthi capabilities in Sana'a, Al Hudaydah, Amran, and Saada provinces amidst intensified fighting.

item.title: Four tankers damaged by sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz within 24 hours
item.description: The fourth tanker in the eastern Strait of Hormuz was severely damaged by a sea mine, causing a fire onboard, according to IRNA. The tanker was in a restricted navigation area with its systems turned off. This marks the fourth such incident in the region within 24 hours, raising concerns about maritime security.

item.title: Kazakhstan Schools to Develop Anti-Terrorism Security Passports Within 45 Days
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Education has mandated that all schools and kindergartens develop anti-terrorism security passports within 45 working days. The new regulations categorize educational facilities into two security groups, with stricter requirements for larger institutions. Schools with over 700 students and staff will require turnstiles and private security.

item.title: World Bank Recommends Gradual Phase-Out of Kazakhstan's '7-20-25' Housing Program
item.description: The World Bank suggests Kazakhstan gradually phase out its '7-20-25' preferential mortgage program. Experts argue that state intervention distorts the market, causing housing prices to rise while market mortgages become more expensive. They recommend reducing state funding and focusing on targeted assistance for citizens in need.

item.title: China's Xi Jinping Addresses APEC Summit, Calls for Post-War Order and WTO Reform
item.description: At the APEC Business Summit in Shenzhen, Chinese President Xi Jinping urged Asia-Pacific nations to firmly support the post-war international order and multipolarity. He advocated for reforming the World Trade Organization and promoting inclusive globalization, emphasizing dialogue and cooperation to overcome challenges.

item.title: 4,950-Apartment Mortgage Housing Complex Under Construction in Kara-Balta
item.description: A housing complex with 4,950 apartments across 66 blocks is being built in Kara-Balta. The State Mortgage Company reports that monolithic work is complete on 20 blocks, with facade and interior finishing underway. The project includes social infrastructure like a school, kindergarten, and parking.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Fruit Exports Plummet, Russia Remains Top Buyer Despite Reductions
item.description: Kazakhstan's fruit exports fell by nearly half in January-September 2026 compared to the previous year, totaling 111,000 tons worth $26.7 million. Exports of peaches, apricots, plums, and cherries saw a significant 6.8-fold decrease. Russia remains the primary destination, though its purchases also declined.

item.title: Kazakh President Returns Law on State Awards to Kurultai with Objections
item.description: For the first time, the Kazakh President has returned a passed law to the Kurultai with objections. The amendments concern the law 'On State Awards of the Republic of Kazakhstan'. The President can now return laws for reconsideration if they raise concerns, with the Kurultai able to override objections.

item.title: Kazakh Businesses Hesitate to Take Loans Despite Falling Interest Rates
item.description: Kazakh companies are seeking loans at an average of 18% annually but consider 7.9% acceptable, a gap explaining low borrowing for development. Banks approve nine out of ten applications, yet demand remains modest. The National Bank's key rate has decreased since June, but businesses are reluctant to borrow.

item.title: Homebuyers Urge Kyrgyz Government to Complete Unfinished Residential Complexes
item.description: Homebuyers of unfinished residential complexes from the "Rayan Building" construction company have appealed to the Kyrgyz Minister of Construction, Nurdani Oryntayev. They requested the state take over and complete the projects with government support. Ministry specialists will assess the sites to determine feasibility.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Security Council and UNDP Strengthen Partnership
item.description: Adilet Orozbekov, Secretary of the Security Council of Kyrgyzstan, met with Alexandra Solovyeva, UNDP Resident Representative in Kyrgyzstan. They reaffirmed their commitment to long-term cooperation, focusing on strengthening national security, enhancing institutional stability, and developing interagency mechanisms.

item.title: HRW Warns ICC Decision Jeopardizes Justice for Afghan Victims
item.description: Human Rights Watch warns the International Criminal Court's decision to close parts of its Afghanistan investigation may hinder victims' access to justice. The ruling restricts investigations into alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity by the Taliban, ISKP, former Afghan forces, and others. Only the Taliban's alleged crimes post-August 2021 remain open.

item.title: Two Casinos for Foreigners Only Planned in East Kazakhstan
item.description: Two casinos exclusively for foreign tourists are planned for construction in the Zaisan and Markakol districts of East Kazakhstan, near the Chinese border. Construction preparations have begun. Kazakh citizens will not be allowed entry; only foreign tourists and staff will have access. The project aims to attract foreign visitors.

item.title: Three Service Points Under Construction on North-South Alternative Road
item.description: Three modern road service points are being built at kilometer markers 107, 260, and 357 of the North-South alternative road in Kyrgyzstan. The Transport and Communications Ministry reports that construction is ongoing, aiming to improve road maintenance infrastructure and ensure continuous service in various weather conditions.

item.title: Cheese Plant Worth 35 Billion Tenge to Be Built on Returned Land in Konayev
item.description: A cheese production plant valued at 35.2 billion tenge is planned for construction in Konayev, Kazakhstan, on land recently returned to state ownership. This is part of a larger initiative to develop five enterprises on reclaimed lands, collectively costing 60.2 billion tenge and expected to create around 700 jobs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sees Rise in Human Trafficking Cases, Official Data Shows
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has reported an increase in human trafficking cases, with figures rising from 6 in 2021 to 20 in 2024. While no cases of parents selling children were recorded in the first nine months of 2026, criminal cases involving such acts are under investigation. The Interior Ministry's Criminal Investigations Department highlighted the issue, emphasizing the need for legal and informational literacy to prevent citizens from becoming victims abroad.

item.title: China's Record Party Purge Driven by Control, Not Just Corruption
item.description: China's Communist Party has expelled a record 33 officials from its Central Committee, a move analysts suggest is primarily aimed at consolidating control and ensuring loyalty ahead of the 2027 congress, rather than solely combating corruption. While corruption is a real issue, the scale of the purge, including former Politburo members and generals, indicates a focus on securing power and eliminating potential threats to leadership.

item.title: Ebola Outbreak in Eastern Congo Remains Uncontrolled, Cases and Deaths Rise Sharply
item.description: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo is uncontrolled, with cases and deaths rising at record rates. Over 11,000 infected and 5,500 deaths reported since May 15. The outbreak is twice as fast as the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic, facing challenges from instability and mistrust.

item.title: Tajikistan Waives Import Duties on Fuel from Non-Free Trade Zone Countries Until 2026
item.description: The government of Tajikistan has established a zero import customs duty rate for petroleum products and gases from countries not participating in the Free Trade Zone Agreement. This measure will be in effect until the end of 2026. The decision aims to reduce the cost of fuel imports from specific nations.

item.title: US Midterm Elections Could Shift Washington's Policy Towards Pakistan's Military Leadership
item.description: The recent US midterm elections may alter Washington's approach to Pakistan, as the Democratic party gains control of committees overseeing aid and arms sales. This comes amid concerns about Pakistan's military tightening its grip on democratic institutions and past human rights abuses.

item.title: China Consortium to Build Gas Processing Plant in Kazakhstan
item.description: Kazakhstan's QazaqGaz has signed a contract with a Chinese consortium to construct a gas processing plant with a capacity of 2.5 billion cubic meters annually, sourced from the Kashagan field. The project's estimated cost exceeds $2.5 billion. This deal is part of a series of significant energy sector wins for Chinese companies in the region this year.

item.title: Biden Claims He Was Assured Kabul Would Last Six Months Post-Withdrawal
item.description: Former US President Joe Biden stated in his memoir that military and intelligence officials assured him Kabul would remain under government control for at least six months after troop withdrawal. He also claims assurances about airport security proved false, referencing the Abbey Gate bombing. Biden defends his decision to end the war, asserting he would make the same choice again.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Foreign Investor Protection with New Agreement
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office and the American Chamber of Commerce (AmCham Kazakhstan) have signed a memorandum to enhance foreign investor rights protection. The agreement aims to strengthen cooperation, identify and eliminate systemic barriers to investment, and improve pre-trial dispute resolution mechanisms.

item.title: One-year-old child dies from measles in Kazakhstan amid vaccination debate
item.description: A one-year-old child has died from measles in the Atyrau region of Kazakhstan. Health officials confirmed the death, which occurred after the child was transferred to a regional infectious disease hospital. The child's parents reportedly refused vaccination, citing a congenital heart defect and advice from a cardiac surgeon.

item.title: Uzbekistan officially bans sexual harassment in the workplace
item.description: Uzbekistan has officially banned sexual harassment in the workplace by amending its Labor Code. The new article defines sexual harassment as unwelcome actions of a sexual nature that demean a person's honor and dignity. Employers are now obligated to create an environment free from such harassment.

item.title: UN Approves $18 Million in Aid for Vulnerable Afghans Ahead of Winter
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) has approved $18 million in emergency funding to assist over 824,000 vulnerable people in Afghanistan. The aid, allocated through the Central Emergency Response Fund, will support projects in food security, healthcare, and sanitation, aiming to prevent deaths and illness during the approaching winter and lean season.

item.title: Uzbek President Concludes State Visit to Oman, Signing Strategic Partnership Agreement
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has concluded his state visit to the Sultanate of Oman. During the visit, he held talks with Sultan Haitham bin Tarik and met with business leaders, resulting in a Strategic Partnership Agreement and over 30 other documents. A portfolio of projects worth $5 billion was formed.

item.title: Kabul Appoints Four New Diplomats to Afghanistan's Missions in Germany
item.description: Taliban authorities have reportedly appointed four additional diplomats to Afghanistan's diplomatic missions in Germany, with nominees traveling to Qatar for visas. Sources suggest these officials are set to take up positions at the embassy in Berlin and the consulate in Bonn. German authorities have reportedly agreed to issue visas, though official confirmation is pending.

item.title: Ashgabat to Host International Transport Conference and Exhibition in November
item.description: Ashgabat will host the international conference and exhibition "International Transport Corridors: Connectivity and Development - 2026" and the "Turkmentel - 2026" exhibition from November 24-26. The event aims to discuss global transport architecture, foster international cooperation, and promote transport diplomacy to expand trade and investment.

item.title: Iran Reports US Strike on Qeshm Island in Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran has reported that the United States conducted a strike on facilities on the Iranian island of Qeshm on November 17. The deputy governor of Hormozgan province stated that residential, commercial, and infrastructure facilities were not affected. The nature of the targeted objects remains unspecified by Iranian authorities.

item.title: Uzbekistan Considers Easing Visa Procedures with Canada
item.description: Uzbekistan's Presidential Administration head, Saida Mirziyoyeva, met with Canadian Ambassador Christopher Dagan to discuss expanding trade, investment, and educational cooperation, including easing visa procedures. Mirziyoyeva expressed confidence that joint initiatives will elevate mutual relations and create opportunities for citizens.

item.title: Pakistan Invites Turkmenistan to Join Central Asia-South Asia Electricity Project
item.description: Pakistan has invited Turkmenistan to join the CASA-1000 electricity transmission project, aiming to boost electricity trade between Central and South Asia. Pakistan's energy minister discussed the proposal with his Turkmen counterpart, also suggesting extending the transmission line to Uzbekistan. Pakistan seeks to address its energy shortages and develop its economy through these regional power projects.

item.title: New Compressor at Kazakhstan's Karachaganak Field to Maintain Production Levels
item.description: A sixth gas compressor has been commissioned at the Karachaganak field in Kazakhstan's West Kazakhstan region, capable of reinjecting up to 4 billion cubic meters of gas annually. This measure aims to maintain reservoir pressure and sustain oil production at 10-11 million tons per year. The project involved local employment and a significant share of Kazakhstani goods and services.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Test Self-Driving Vehicles on Astana Roads
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to test self-driving vehicles on designated routes in Astana as part of a three-year pilot project. The relevant draft decree is open for public discussion until December 2. Previously, driverless taxi services were planned for Astana, Almaty, and the Akmola region.

item.title: Ashgabat Hosts OSCE Parliamentary Assembly Meeting on Neutrality and Diplomacy
item.description: The third high-level Ashgabat meeting of the OSCE Parliamentary Assembly on neutrality and parliamentary diplomacy commenced today. Organized jointly by the Mejlis of Turkmenistan and the OSCE, the forum brings together parliamentary leaders and representatives from member states and international organizations.
